description: 12-week plan building from basic fitness to completing a 10K.

weeks.weekGoal: Introduction to run/walk intervals - build base fitness

days.cardioNotes: 8 rounds of: 1 min jog, 2 min walk. Focus on easy, conversational jogging pace.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
exercises.notes: Focus on depth and control, keep chest up

exercises.name: Pushup (knees OK)
exercises.notes: Modify to knees if needed, maintain straight line

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.notes: Each leg, focus on balance and control

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.notes: 30 seconds each set, maintain neutral spine

days.cardioNotes: 8 rounds of: 1 min jog, 2 min walk. Same as Monday, focus on consistency.
8 rounds of: 1 min jog, 2 min walk. End of week 1 - you should feel stronger!

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
exercises.notes: Focus on depth and control, keep chest up

exercises.name: Pushup (knees OK)
exercises.notes: Modify to knees if needed, maintain straight line

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.notes: Each leg, focus on balance and control

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.notes: 30 seconds each set, maintain neutral spine

weeks.weekGoal: Increase running intervals - build aerobic capacity

days.cardioNotes: 6 rounds of: 90 sec jog, 2 min walk. Longer running intervals this week.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
exercises.notes: Focus on depth and control, keep chest up

exercises.name: Pushup (knees OK)
exercises.notes: Modify to knees if needed, maintain straight line

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.notes: Each leg, focus on balance and control

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Squeeze glutes at top, hold 2 seconds

days.cardioNotes: 6 rounds of: 90 sec jog, 2 min walk. Keep pace conversational.
6 rounds of: 90 sec jog, 2 min walk. Notice how much easier this feels than week 1!

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
exercises.notes: Focus on depth and control, keep chest up

exercises.name: Pushup (knees OK)
exercises.notes: Modify to knees if needed, maintain straight line

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.notes: Each leg, focus on balance and control

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Squeeze glutes at top, hold 2 seconds

days.cardioNotes: 5 rounds of: 2 min jog, 2 min walk. Equal work and rest - building endurance.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: Use light weight (10-15 lbs), focus on depth

exercises.name: Pushup
exercises.notes: From toes if possible, knees OK

days.cardioNotes: 5 rounds of: 2 min jog, 2 min walk. Keep it controlled and conversational.
5 rounds of: 2 min jog, 2 min walk. Halfway through base phase!

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: Use light weight (10-15 lbs), focus on depth

exercises.name: Pushup
exercises.notes: From toes if possible, knees OK

weeks.weekGoal: Recovery week - consolidate gains before progression

days.cardioNotes: 6 rounds of: 90 sec jog, 2 min walk. Easier week to recover and adapt.
6 rounds of: 90 sec jog, 2 min walk. Enjoy this lighter week.
6 rounds of: 90 sec jog, 2 min walk. Ready for continuous running next!

weeks.weekGoal: Building continuous running - reduce walk breaks
weeks.keyWorkouts: 3x run sessions with short walk breaks, 2x strength

days.cardioNotes: 4 rounds of: 5 min jog, 1 min walk. Longer running intervals now!
4 rounds of: 5 min jog, 1 min walk. Keep pace easy and sustainable.
4 rounds of: 5 min jog, 1 min walk. You're running more than walking now!
20 minute continuous run. No walk breaks! Keep it easy and conversational.
25 minute continuous run. Building endurance steadily.
30 minute continuous run! Major milestone - you can run for 30 minutes straight! Base phase complete.
30 minute easy run. Conversational pace.
35 minute run. Start easy, last 10 min at moderate effort.
30 minute easy run. Recovery-paced.
45 minute long run covering ~4 miles. Easy conversational pace throughout.
35 minute easy run. Keep it conversational.
40 minute run. First 30 min easy, last 10 min at moderate effort.
30 minute easy recovery run.
55 minute long run covering ~5 miles. You're getting close to 10K distance!
30 minute easy run. Recovery week - keep it light.
30 minute easy run. Enjoy the lighter week.
25 minute easy run. Absorb the training.
45 minute long run. Easy conversational pace. Recovery week.
35 minute easy run. Build back up after recovery week.
40 minute run. First 30 min easy, last 10 min at moderate-hard effort.
30 minute easy recovery run.
70 minute long run covering 6+ miles. You're ready for 10K distance! Keep it easy and conversational.
35 minute easy run. Save energy for the long run.
40 minute run. Easy for 30 min, last 10 min at moderate effort.
30 minute easy run. Final prep before full 10K.
Full 10K distance (6.2 miles)! This is your peak long run. Keep it conversational and complete the distance. You've got this!
Easy 25 minute run. Keep it light and comfortable - you're tapering for race day!
Short 20 minute easy run. Include 3-4 x 20 second strides at the end to keep legs sharp.

10K RACE DAY! You've trained for 12 weeks and you're ready! Goal: Complete 10K (65-70 minutes, 10:30-11:00/mile pace). Start conservatively, settle into a comfortable rhythm, and finish strong. Trust the process and enjoy the accomplishment!
